the volatile compound composition, lipid oxidation, and sensory quality of steamed yellow tail fish muscle deteriorated when the fish was stored for 3 days before reheated, while the nutritional value of the fish was not affected by the storage.

the volatile compound compositions and lipid oxidation of yellowtail fish muscle steamed and then reheated after refrigeration storage of up to three days are not significantly different from those of steamed fish muscle only once, except that some volatiles were higher in the reheated samples.
the quality of yellowtail steamed meat was maintained during refrigerated storage for 3 days before reheated.

reheating after storage of 7 days is not recommended.
steamed fish meat reheated after 3 days of storage could be consumed without any deterioration of its quality.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the storage period before reheated steamed yellowtail muscle has an effect on the volatile composition, lipid oxidation, and sensory properties.
the storage period before reheated steamed fish meat affects the volatile compound composition, lipid oxidation and odor.
the quality of steamed yellow tail fish meat was affected by storage time, and the quality deterioration of the meat was accelerated by reheating after storage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reheating steamed fish meat after refrigerated storage for up to 3 days is acceptable for consumption.
the storage period of steamed yellowtails should be limited to 3 day before reheating to ensure the quality of the meat.
steamed yellowtail muscle reheated after refrigeration storage of up to three days can be consumed without deterioration in its odor and nutritional value.
